Checks each union field after normalization and accepts only references, recursively permitted tuples/arrays, `ManuallyDrop`, `Copy`, or erroneous types; otherwise emits an invalid-union-field error. It calls the nested helper `allowed_union_field` to recursively classify field types.

Recursively decides whether a type is legal as a union field: references are accepted, tuples and arrays are checked recursively, and other types are accepted only if they are `ManuallyDrop`, `Copy`, or already erroneous. It calls itself recursively for tuple elements and array elements.

Computes the layout of a static to reject oversized foreign statics and lint uninhabited static types, while treating unexpected layout failures as delayed bugs. It does not call other listed methods.

Validates an opaque type item by confirming it is an opaque HIR item, skipping rustdoc, bailing out on erroneous hidden types, then calling `check_opaque_for_cycles` and, if that succeeds, `check_opaque_meets_bounds`.

Detects invalid recursive opaque expansions by trying impl-trait expansion with and without coroutine fields, reporting a true opaque cycle via `opaque_type_cycle_error`, and otherwise checking for coroutine layout cycles. It calls `opaque_type_cycle_error` when a real expansion cycle is found.

Builds an inference and obligation context for an opaque type, relates the declared opaque to its hidden type under the proper parameter environment, registers well-formedness and bound obligations, and reports fulfillment or region-resolution errors if the hidden type does not satisfy the opaque's bounds. It does not call other listed methods.

Dispatches item-type validation by `DefKind`: for statics it calls `check_static_inhabited` and `check_static_linkage`; for enums it calls `check_enum`; for trait impls it calls `check_impl_items_against_trait` and `check_on_unimplemented` when coherence succeeds; for traits it calls `check_on_unimplemented`; for structs it calls `check_struct`; for unions it calls `check_union`; and for opaque types it calls `check_opaque_precise_captures` before further opaque-origin-specific validation. This is the central coordinator for the file’s item-level checks.
Forces evaluation of a trait or impl item's `#[rustc_on_unimplemented]` directive so any diagnostic errors are reported. It does not call other listed methods.

Walks ancestor impls to determine whether an impl item is allowed to specialize a trait item, rejecting specialization when the inherited parent item is final or comes from a non-default ancestor impl. It does not call other listed methods.

Checks each impl item against its corresponding trait item, dispatching to the appropriate impl-vs-trait comparison and then calling `check_specialization_validity`; it also performs follow-up validation for missing items and inherited defaults across trait ancestors. It calls `check_specialization_validity` for every matched impl item.

Validates a SIMD struct by requiring at least one field, homogeneous element types, a legal lane count, and scalar-or-pointer lane element kinds (or generic forms deferred to monomorphization). It does not call other listed methods.

Validates `repr(packed)` usage by rejecting conflicting packed hints or `packed`+`align`, and otherwise checking for transitive containment of `repr(align)` types. It calls `check_packed_inner` to search nested field types for aligned ADTs.

Recursively searches a struct/union and its nested ADT fields for a `repr(align)` type while tracking a stack to avoid cycles, returning the path of offending definitions and field spans when found. It calls itself recursively on nested ADT field types.

Validates `repr(transparent)` ADTs by enforcing the feature gate for transparent unions, requiring exactly one variant, computing which fields are trivial 1-ZSTs, and rejecting invalid transparent layouts including problematic non-exhaustive/private external ZST contents. It calls the nested helper `check_non_exhaustive` to recursively inspect field types for disallowed external non-exhaustive/private structure.

Recursively inspects a type used in a transparent field and stops when it finds a non-local ADT whose variant/field set is non-exhaustive or contains private fields; tuples, arrays, and nested ADT fields are traversed recursively. It calls itself recursively for tuple elements, array elements, and nested ADT field types.

Performs enum validation by forcing destructor evaluation, rejecting `repr` on zero-variant enums, feature-gating `repr(i128/u128)`, type-checking explicit discriminants, enforcing `#[repr(inttype)]` when mixed explicit discriminants require it, then calling `detect_discriminant_duplicate` and `check_transparent`.

Detects duplicate enum discriminant values and builds detailed diagnostics that explain whether the duplicate was explicit, overflow-derived, or inherited from a prior explicit discriminant. It does not call other listed methods.

Constructs the diagnostic for an opaque-type recursion error by examining return paths, distinguishing pure-`!` returns from recursive opaque uses, and tracing recursive references through nested opaque types and closures/coroutines. It uses the nested `OpaqueTypeCollector::visit_ty` visitor to collect opaque and closure/coroutine references from return types.

Checks that an opaque type definition does not capture parent lifetimes or illicit `Self` references from its surrounding context, walking both the HIR item and the opaque’s explicit bounds. It calls `expect_item` to fetch the HIR item, `mk_opaque`, `identity_for_item`, `generics_of`, and `explicit_item_bounds` to construct and inspect the opaque identity and bounds, uses `visit_item`, `visit_with`, and `break_value` through local visitors to detect forbidden lifetime capture, uses `def_path_str` while recording `Self`-type references, and reports diagnostics via `span_suggestion`, `unwrap_or_else`, `map_break`, and `emit`.

Visits a region and stops when it finds an early-bound lifetime inherited from a parent generics scope; otherwise it continues recursively. It calls `super_visit_with` when the region is not an inherited early-bound lifetime.

Visits a const while intentionally skipping unevaluated consts, since lifetime capture inside their substitutions is not fully checked here. For other consts, it calls `kind` to inspect the const form and `super_visit_with` to continue traversal.

Checks each lowered type for forbidden parent-lifetime capture, but ignores the opaque type’s own identity to avoid self-matching. For other types, it calls `super_visit_with` with `FindParentLifetimeVisitor` and then `map_break` to convert a found parent lifetime into the offending type.
Supplies the HIR map used for nested body traversal by this visitor. It calls `hir` to obtain that map from the type context.

Walks HIR type syntax to collect `Self` type references that are illegal to capture inside the opaque definition, recording either plain `Self` or aliased `Self` paths. It calls `def_path_str` to name aliased `Self` targets, `push` to record each match, and `walk_ty` to continue recursive HIR traversal.

Verifies that all type parameters declared on a top-level generic item are actually used in the item type, suppressing the check if the type already contains an error. It calls `own_counts` and `len` to size the tracking set, `references_error`, `has_errors`, and `is_some` to short-circuit on prior errors, `walk`, `unpack`, and `kind` to inspect type leaves, `insert` and `contains` to track used parameters, `def_span` to locate unused ones, and `span_label` plus `emit` to report E0091.
Checks every item type in a module by iterating over the module’s HIR items. It calls `hir_module_items`, `items`, and `check_item_type`.

Emits the dedicated recursion error for an `async fn` whose opaque future type forms a cycle and therefore requires boxing. It calls `span_label`, `note`, and `emit` to build and issue the diagnostic.

Traverses a type to collect nested opaque type definitions referenced within it. It calls `kind` to detect `ty::Opaque`, `push` to record each opaque def-id found, and `super_visit_with` to recurse into non-opaque types.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir_typeck/src/check.rs::: Type-checks a function body by preparing the `FnCtxt` state, replacing opaque return types with inference variables, forbidding invalid intrinsic ABIs, gathering locals, checking parameter patterns and well-formedness, enforcing sizedness constraints, checking the body, and reconciling the coerced body result with the declared return type; it explicitly calls `forbid_intrinsic_abi` and uses `GatherLocalsVisitor::new(...).visit_body(...)` to collect locals before parameter/body checking.

Validates that the panic handler lang item has the required non-generic function form by constructing the expected `for<'a, 'b> fn(&'a PanicInfo<'b>) -> !` signature and explicitly calling `check_function_signature` to compare it against the actual signature.

Validates the signature and generic-parameter restrictions of an `#[alloc_error_handler]` function. It calls `tcx.lang_items().alloc_layout()` to fetch the required `Layout` lang item, uses `declared_ret_ty.kind()` to require a `!` return type, calls `fn_sig.inputs()` and `len()` to enforce exactly one argument, checks whether the sole argument is the `Layout` ADT via `kind()` and `did()`, calls `tcx.def_kind(fn_id)` to require that the item is a function, and calls `tcx.generics_of(fn_id).own_counts()` to ensure there are no type or const parameters. On each failure path it emits diagnostics through `err`, `span_err`, and span lookups such as `decl.output.span()` and `tcx.def_span(fn_id)`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_infer/src/infer/opaque_ty: Scans a foldable value for local opaque aliases that are currently definable in this context, replaces each eligible opaque with a fresh inference type variable, and accumulates the resulting obligations. It first short-circuits when `next_trait_solver` is enabled or `has_opaque_types` is false, and for each matched opaque it calls `opaque_type_origin` to decide eligibility and `handle_opaque_type` to relate the new inference variable back to the opaque definition.

Handles the relation between an opaque type and another type during inference, ignoring error types, orienting the comparison by `a_is_expected`, and only treating local opaque aliases as definitional when they are valid for the current `DefiningAnchor`. When the opaque is allowed to be defined here, it calls `opaque_type_origin` to validate the defining context and then calls `register_hidden_type` to record the inferred hidden type; otherwise it emits diagnostics for invalid defining-use situations such as problematic opaque-to-opaque cases.

Resolves the concrete hidden type, computes the invariant lifetime arguments of the opaque plus `'static` as the allowed choice set, and visits the hidden type to constrain every free region to one of those choices. It calls `member_constraint` through the region visitor callback for each discovered region.

Determines whether a local opaque type is being defined from the current defining-use anchor and, if so, returns its `OpaqueTyOrigin`. For type-alias opaques it checks associated-type definitions via `opaque_types_defined_by` and otherwise calls `may_define_opaque_type` to decide whether the current item may define the opaque.
Returns whether this `UseKind` represents a defining use, yielding true for `DefiningUse` and false for `OpaqueUse`.

Registers an inferred hidden type for an opaque definition and produces the obligations needed to justify it. It calls `insert_hidden_type` to store or unify the hidden type in the opaque-type table, then calls `add_item_bounds_for_hidden_type` to add the opaque item's declared bounds as obligations on that hidden type.
Checks whether a named opaque type may be defined from the given local item by walking up the HIR parent chain from the item to see whether it reaches the opaque type’s defining scope.

Looks up the HIR item for a local opaque type definition and returns its `OpaqueTyOrigin`; it calls `self.tcx.hir().expect_item(def_id)` to fetch the item and triggers a span bug if the item is not an opaque type.
Visits the contents of a binder without special casing it, delegating traversal to `t.super_visit_with(self)` and then continuing.
Processes each region seen by the visitor, ignoring late-bound regions and invoking the visitor callback `self.op` for all other regions before continuing.

Traverses only types that contain free regions and skips enclosing-item lifetime parameters for closures and generators. For closures it calls `substs.as_closure().tupled_upvars_ty().visit_with(self)` and `substs.as_closure().sig_as_fn_ptr_ty().visit_with(self)`; for generators it calls `substs.as_generator().tupled_upvars_ty().visit_with(self)`, `return_ty().visit_with(self)`, `yield_ty().visit_with(self)`, and `resume_ty().visit_with(self)`; otherwise it falls back to `ty.super_visit_with(self)`.

Reverts a previously logged opaque-type change for `key`: if a prior `OpaqueHiddenType` is provided, it restores that hidden type in the existing declaration; otherwise it removes the declaration entirely and bugs if the key was never registered. It does not call any other method from the provided Methods List.
Drains and returns the entire stored `OpaqueTypeMap` by taking it out of `self`, leaving the storage empty. It does not call any other method from the provided Methods List.

Constructs and returns an `OpaqueTypeTable` view that pairs this storage with the given undo log so later mutations can be recorded for snapshot rollback. It does not call any other method from the provided Methods List.

On drop, checks whether any opaque-type entries remain in storage and, if so, emits a delayed compiler bug containing the leftover map to enforce that inference state was fully drained. It does not call any other method from the provided Methods List.

Registers or updates the opaque-type declaration for `key`: if an entry already exists, it replaces the stored hidden type, logs `UndoLog::OpaqueTypes(key, Some(prev))`, and returns the previous concrete `Ty`; otherwise it inserts a new `OpaqueTypeDecl`, logs `UndoLog::OpaqueTypes(key, None)`, and returns `None`. It does not call any other method from the provided Methods List.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_middle/src/ty/opaque_type: Constructs a `ReverseMapper` from the type context, remapping table, diagnostic span, and error-suppression flag, initializing `do_not_error` to `false`. It does not call other methods from the Methods List.

Temporarily enables the `do_not_error` mode, folds a generic argument through this mapper, and then restores normal error behavior. It calls `fold_with` on the argument, which routes folding back through this `TypeFolder` implementation.

Folds a generic argument through the mapper under normal diagnostics, requiring that missing-region suppression is not active. It calls `fold_with` on the argument, which uses this `TypeFolder` implementation.
Returns the `TyCtxt` stored in `ReverseMapper`; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.

Remaps opaque-type regions by leaving late-bound, `'static`, and erased regions unchanged, validating that only expected region kinds are processed, and then looking up named regions in the reverse map. If a mapped lifetime is found it returns it; if no mapping exists it either substitutes `'static` when missing-region errors are suppressed or emits the defining-scope opaque-type diagnostic and falls back to `'static`. This method calls `tcx` from the Methods List to obtain the fallback `'static` lifetime in the error path.

Remaps types inside the hidden type, with special handling for closure- and generator-like types: for parent generic arguments it tolerates missing-region mappings, while for the remaining arguments it performs normal remapping, then rebuilds the closure/generator with the rewritten substitutions. For type parameters, it replaces them from the reverse map or reports an error and yields a type error when unmapped; all other types are recursively folded. This method calls `fold_kind_no_missing_regions_error` and `fold_kind_normally` from the same impl to rewrite closure/generator arguments, and otherwise falls back to recursive folding via `super_fold_with`.

Remaps const generic parameters by looking them up in the reverse map and returning the corresponding opaque-type const argument. If a const parameter is unmapped, it optionally emits `ConstNotUsedTraitAlias` and returns a const error; non-parameter consts are left unchanged. This method calls `tcx` from the Methods List to construct the fallback const error.
Walks all item-like nodes in the given module and triggers collection by calling `hir` and `visit_item_likes_in_module` with `CollectItemTypesVisitor`.
Registers collect-phase query providers into `Providers` and delegates to `resolve_bound_vars::provide` to install bound-variable related queries before filling this file’s query entries.
Records the span of inferred placeholder types (`_`) encountered in a type node, then calls `intravisit::walk_ty` to continue traversing nested type structure.

Checks generic arguments for inferred placeholders, recording their spans; for inferred args it calls `intravisit::walk_inf`, and for type args it explicitly calls `visit_ty` to reuse type placeholder handling.
Records the span of inferred array lengths and then calls `intravisit::walk_array_len` to visit nested array-length structure.

Emits a placeholder-type diagnostic for item signatures when any placeholder spans were collected; if spans exist, it calls `placeholder_type_error_diag` and then emits the returned diagnostic with `.emit()`.

Builds the detailed diagnostic for illegal placeholder types in item signatures, including generic-parameter replacement suggestions and special handling for bare functions in const/static contexts. It calls `bad_placeholder` to create the base diagnostic and may call `tcx.parent_hir_node` and `multipart_suggestion` when forming suggestions.

Rejects placeholder types in supported item signatures by selecting the item’s generics/suggestion mode, visiting the item with `HirPlaceholderCollector::visit_item`, and then calling `placeholder_type_error` with the collected spans.
Returns the HIR map from `self.tcx.hir()` for nested visitor traversal.

For each item, forces signature-level lowering by calling `lower_item`, checks item signatures for placeholder types via `reject_placeholder_type_signatures_in_item`, and then calls `intravisit::walk_item` to recurse into nested HIR.

Ensures type information for generic parameter defaults is collected: it calls `self.tcx.ensure().type_of` for type defaults and const parameters, calls `self.tcx.ensure().const_param_default` for const defaults, and finally calls `intravisit::walk_generics` to continue traversal.

When encountering a closure expression, forces collection of closure generics and codegen attributes by calling `self.tcx.ensure().generics_of` and `self.tcx.ensure().codegen_fn_attrs`, then calls `intravisit::walk_expr` to visit nested expressions.
Forces lowering of each trait item by calling `lower_trait_item`, then calls `intravisit::walk_trait_item` to traverse inside the trait item.
Forces lowering of each impl item by calling `lower_impl_item`, then calls `intravisit::walk_impl_item` to traverse inside the impl item.
Creates the base diagnostic for placeholder types in item signatures by pluralizing the item kind, sorting spans, and calling `tcx.dcx().create_err` with the placeholder error payload.
Constructs a new `ItemCtxt` with the given type context and item `LocalDefId`, initializing error taint tracking to empty.
Lowers an HIR type into a rustc `Ty` by calling `astconv` and then `ast_ty_to_ty`.
Returns the HIR id for the current item by calling `self.tcx.local_def_id_to_hir_id(self.item_def_id)`.
Fetches the current HIR node for this item by calling `self.hir_id()` and then `self.tcx.hir_node(...)`.
Returns the underlying type context stored in the item context; it does not call other listed methods.
Returns the current item as a global `DefId` by calling `to_def_id` on the local item id.
Fetches generic predicates for an associated type parameter at a span by calling `at` and then `type_param_predicates` on `tcx`.
Disables region inference in item collection by always returning `None`; it does not call other listed methods.
Reports that placeholder type inference is not allowed during this collection phase by always returning `false`; it does not call other listed methods.
Creates an error type for an illegal placeholder type by calling `tcx` and `new_error_with_message`.
Creates an error constant for an illegal placeholder const after normalizing regions by calling `fold_regions`, `tcx`, and `new_error_with_message`.

Builds a projected associated type from a poly trait reference. In the simple case it calls `no_bound_vars`, `astconv`, `create_args_for_associated_item`, `tcx`, and `new_projection`; in the late-bound-region error path it also queries HIR and emits a diagnostic, eventually returning an error type.
Ignores the tainted-by-errors signal during item collection; it does not call other listed methods.
No-op hook for recording signature types; it does not call other listed methods.

Chooses a fresh lifetime name not already used by the referenced late-bound regions or the HIR generics, first collecting existing names via `collect_referenced_late_bound_regions` and then scanning generated `'a`, `'b`, … candidates until one is unused.

Collects signature-level information for a top-level HIR item by matching its kind and forcing the appropriate queries. Depending on the item, it calls `hir`, `item`, `foreign_item`, `ensure`, `generics_of`, `type_of`, `predicates_of`, `codegen_fn_attrs`, `fn_sig`, `placeholder_type_error`, `convert_enum_variant_types`, `trait_def`, `at`, `super_predicates_of`, `implied_predicates_of`, `convert_variant_ctor`, `explicit_item_bounds`, and `item_bounds`.

Collects type information for a trait item, always forcing `generics_of` first and `predicates_of` last. Depending on the trait item kind, it calls `hir`, `trait_item`, `ensure`, `codegen_fn_attrs`, `type_of`, `fn_sig`, `item_bounds`, `is_suggestable_infer_ty`, and `placeholder_type_error`.

Collects signature information for an impl item by forcing `generics_of`, `type_of`, and `predicates_of`, then handling kind-specific work. It calls `hir`, `impl_item`, `ensure`, `codegen_fn_attrs`, `fn_sig`, `is_suggestable_infer_ty`, and `placeholder_type_error`.
Forces collection of a variant constructor by calling `ensure`, `generics_of`, `type_of`, and `predicates_of`.

Computes enum variant discriminants, reports overflow, and forces field and constructor collection for each variant. It calls `adt_def`, `repr`, `discr_type`, `initial_discriminant`, `variants`, `map_or`, `wrap_incr`, `eval_explicit_discr`, `disr_incr`, `def_span`, `emit_err`, `item_name`, `ensure`, `generics_of`, `type_of`, `predicates_of`, `ctor_def_id`, `expect_local`, and `convert_variant_ctor`.

Builds a `ty::VariantDef` from HIR variant data, checking for duplicate field names and collecting field metadata. It calls `fields`, `iter`, `map`, `get`, `normalize_to_macros_2_0`, `cloned`, `emit_err`, `insert`, `to_def_id`, `visibility`, `collect`, `ctor`, `has_attr`, and constructs the result with `new`.

Builds the compiler’s `ty::AdtDef` for a local enum, struct, union, or anonymous ADT. It inherits repr options from the parent ADT for anonymous fields or uses `repr_options_of_def` otherwise, lowers each enum variant or the single struct/union body by calling `lower_variant`, and finally constructs the ADT with `mk_adt_def`.

Builds a `ty::TraitDef` from a trait or trait alias item, collecting trait flags, validating special attributes, and extracting attribute-driven metadata such as specialization and must-implement-one-of requirements. It does not call other methods from this methods list.
Returns whether any generic argument contains a suggestable inferred placeholder by iterating the args and calling `is_suggestable_infer_ty` for type arguments.

Recursively checks whether an HIR type contains `_`-like placeholders that are suitable for diagnostics. It calls itself on nested element types and calls `are_suggestable_generic_args` for opaque and path generic arguments.
Returns the function return type only when it is a suggestable inferred type by calling `is_suggestable_infer_ty` on `FnRetTy::Return`.

Computes the polymorphic function signature for local functions, methods, foreign functions, constructors, and closures based on their HIR form. It calls `infer_return_ty_for_fn_sig` for functions whose return type may be inferred, `compute_sig_of_foreign_fn_decl` for foreign functions, and for constructor cases uses `type_of` to build the synthesized constructor signature directly.

Handles function signatures with inferred return types by consulting type checking results, diagnosing illegal placeholders, and recovering with a suggested explicit return type when possible. It may call `suggest_impl_trait` to format an `impl Trait` replacement, and falls back to ordinary lowering by calling `lower_fn_ty` through the item lowerer when no inferred return type is present.

Lowers an impl's optional trait reference into an early-bound `TraitRef`. It creates an `ItemCtxt`, reads the impl HIR, gets the self type with `type_of` and `instantiate_identity`, validates constness with `check_impl_constness` and `is_const_trait_impl_raw`, and then calls `astconv` and `instantiate_mono_trait_ref` before binding the result.
Determines whether an impl is positive, negative, or reservation, while emitting errors for invalid reservation forms. It calls `has_attr`, `hir`, `expect_item`, `map_or`, and `span_err`.
Returns an iterator over lifetime parameters in the given generics that are early-bound by filtering out late-bound lifetimes with `is_late_bound`.

Combines the item’s explicit predicates with inferred outlives predicates into one `GenericPredicates` result. It calls `explicit_predicates_of` and `inferred_outlives_of`, appending the inferred predicates when present.

Computes the signature of a foreign function declaration, using intrinsic unsafety for Rust intrinsics and otherwise `unsafe`, then lowering the declaration and checking the SIMD-in-FFI feature gate. It calls `intrinsic_operation_unsafety` and lowers the signature with `lower_fn_ty` through a fresh `ItemCtxt`.

Looks up the HIR node for `def_id` and returns the generator kind only when the node is a closure expression; it calls `get_by_def_id` to fetch the node, then calls `body` and `generator_kind` on the closure body, otherwise returns `None`.

Returns the input type unchanged for item signatures, intentionally skipping normalization to avoid extra dependencies; despite its trait role, it does not call any other method from the provided Methods List.

Checks whether a local HIR node for the given `DefId` is a `ForeignItem`, returning `true` only for foreign items and bugging on non-local IDs; it does not call any other method from the provided Methods List.

Parses a `#[target_feature(enable = "...")]` attribute, validates requested features against the target and enabled feature gates, emits diagnostics for malformed or unsupported entries, and appends accepted features to `target_features`; it does not call any other method from the provided Methods List.
Maps a textual LLVM linkage name to the corresponding `Linkage` enum and aborts with a fatal error for invalid names; it does not call any other method from the provided Methods List.

Collects and validates codegen-related attributes for a local item, building a `CodegenFnAttrs` record with flags, linkage, target features, ABI-sensitive checks, and diagnostics. It explicitly calls `should_inherit_track_caller` to inherit `#[track_caller]`, `is_foreign_item` when validating foreign-only attributes, `check_target_feature_trait_unsafe` for trait-method `#[target_feature]` safety checks, `from_target_feature` to parse enabled target features, `linkage_by_name` to decode `#[linkage]`, and `check_link_ordinal` to parse `#[link_ordinal]`.

Computes the effective target-feature set used for inline assembly by starting from session unstable features, then merging per-item codegen features and instruction-set adjustments. It explicitly calls `codegen_fn_attrs` to obtain the item's codegen attributes.

Determines whether an impl method should inherit `#[track_caller]` from its corresponding trait method by inspecting the associated trait item’s codegen flags. It explicitly calls `codegen_fn_attrs` on the trait item.

Validates and parses a `#[link_ordinal(...)]` attribute, enforcing feature gating on x86, requiring exactly one unsuffixed integer argument, and returning a `u16` ordinal when valid; it does not call any other method from the provided Methods List.

Emits an error when both `link_name` and `link_ordinal` are present in the same codegen attributes, using the provided span when available; it does not call any other method from the provided Methods List.

Rejects `#[target_feature]` on safe trait-method impl items by inspecting the HIR parent impl and emitting an error when the method belongs to a trait impl and is not `unsafe`; it does not call any other method from the provided Methods List.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir_analysis/src/check/wf: Returns the underlying `ObligationCtxt` by dereferencing `WfCheckingCtxt`; it does not call other methods from the Methods List.
Returns the `TyCtxt` stored in the inference context inside the obligation context; it does not call other methods from the Methods List.
Normalizes a type-foldable value under the current parameter environment, attaching a `WellFormed` obligation cause for diagnostics; it does not call other methods from the Methods List.
Builds and registers a `WellFormed` predicate obligation for a generic argument using the current body and parameter environment. It calls `WfCheckingCtxt::tcx`.

Creates the temporary inference/obligation context used for well-formedness checking, runs the supplied checker closure, solves obligations, computes implied bounds, lints redundant lifetimes, and resolves/report regions with a compatibility path for some implied-bounds cases; it does not call other methods from the Methods List.

Top-level dispatcher that selects the appropriate WF checker for the HIR node kind and then checks each generic parameter. It calls `check_item`, `check_trait_item`, `check_impl_item`, `check_foreign_item`, `check_item_type`, and `check_param_wf`.

Checks item-level well-formedness after precollecting item types, handling impls, functions, statics/consts/type aliases, ADTs, and traits according to item kind. It calls `check_impl`, `check_item_fn`, `check_item_type`, `check_type_defn`, and `check_trait`.
Checks a foreign item after precollecting its type information, validating foreign functions and statics while accepting foreign types unchanged. It calls `check_item_fn` and `check_item_type`.

Checks a trait item by precollecting its types, diagnosing misuse of the trait name as an unboxed self trait object, validating the associated item itself, and also validating synthesized associated types for RPITIT methods. It calls `check_dyn_incompatible_self_trait_by_name` and `check_associated_item`.

Analyzes generic associated types across all associated items of a trait to infer potentially missing outlives bounds by repeatedly intersecting constraints discovered from method signatures and other bounds. It calls `gather_gat_bounds`, `augment_param_env`, `region_known_to_outlive`, and `ty_known_to_outlive`.
